newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India little changed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India little changed in thin trade.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) were little changed in London in market-maker dominated trade and low levels of client demand.
"It was a typical end of account in Bombay and end of week in London," said a broker.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed up 0.38 points at 61.88 points, with the premium over the local market at 13.71 percent after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 28.70 points to 3,139.02.

Among the stars, ITC closed up 88 cents at $8.75/$9.75, despite the suspension of its panel of directors after India's Enforcement Directorate arrested officials in investigations into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Regulations Act.
"There has been some short-covering on this stock," said the broker.

Elswehere, the Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 1.28 points, 1.98 percent, at 66.20, a premium of 26.01 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 7.26 points to a provisional 750.29.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended flat at 90.26 points, a premium of 0.47 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index fell 14.19 points or 0.21 percent to end at 6,587.44.
